name: La Table du Grapiot
tier: THE BERTHS · THE STARS — PUPILLIN, THE BIB BY THE RIVER AT ARBOIS, AND DOLE
recognition: First MICHELIN star in the France 2026 selection (16 March 2026); Gault&Millau 2026: 14.5/20, Table de Chef; Sonzogni Grand de Demain 2026
what_to_order: Bresse poultry, Vin Jaune and morels (or tarragon)|Snails, garlic butter, cancoillotte espuma|Smoked beef tongue|Salmon trout|Rhubarb dessert|Poulsard by the glass
price_range: Menus 60 / 80 / 94 euros (Découverte, Connaisseur, Expérience; seen Oct 2026, Gault&Millau and Petit Futé); MICHELIN €€€
reservation: Essential (Petit Futé); by phone, MICHELIN does not book it
notes: Bresse poultry with Vin Jaune and morels, on the Connaisseur or Expérience menu
verdict: The most exciting table on the slope this year, and still priced like a village restaurant: 60 euros buys the starred kitchen. Gault&Millau 2026 gives 14.5/20 and calls the Bresse hen with morels exemplary. Hours differ between listings, so call before driving, and pair lunch here with a Pupillin cellar visit rather than making it a late dinner run from Lons.
caveat: Closed Monday; Sunday dinner and weekday hours disputed between listings; book by phone; about 30 km from Lons

name: Le Bistronôme
tier: THE STARS — PUPILLIN, THE BIB BY THE RIVER AT ARBOIS, AND DOLE
recognition: MICHELIN Bib Gourmand shown on its live MICHELIN page (Bib since 2023, Bib of the month Oct 2023); Gault&Millau 2026: 13/20, Table de Chef
what_to_order: Planches trout ballottine, morels, Vin Jaune sauce|Veal medallion, polenta, tarragon jus|Pork from a nearby farm|'Au fil du jour' lunch menu|Chocolate dessert|Jura wine list
price_range: Menus about 35-65 euros (seen Oct 2026, Gault&Millau); MICHELIN €€
notes: Planches trout ballottine with morels and oyster mushrooms, Vin Jaune sauce
verdict: The sensible lunch on the slope: the 'Au fil du jour' menu is what MICHELIN calls unbeatable value, and Gault&Millau 2026 rates the kitchen 13/20 and the town's leading table. It is bistro cooking with serious technique, not a tasting-menu event. From November the Thursday dinner goes, so plan Arbois evenings for Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday or Saturday.
caveat: Closed Sunday and Monday, and Thursday evenings November-March; book lunch; about 40 km from Lons
hot_this_month: The Planches trout ballottine with morels in Vin Jaune sauce; from November closed Thursday evenings as well as Sunday and Monday.

name: La Chaumière
tier: THE STARS — PUPILLIN, THE BIB BY THE RIVER AT ARBOIS, AND DOLE
recognition: One MICHELIN star, listed by Jura Tourisme in March 2026 as one of the Jura's three starred tables; Gault&Millau 2026: 13.5/20
what_to_order: Seasonal tasting menu|Smoked eel|Bresse poultry|Hand-dived scallops|Marinated sea bream carpaccio|Veal kidney fricassee with chanterelles|Jura cheeses
price_range: Gastronomic: 120-140 euros a head before drinks (Gault&Millau 2026, seen Oct 2026); bistrot La Bagatelle: MICHELIN €€, no menu prices found
reservation: Essential for the Friday-Saturday gastronomic room; book direct (MICHELIN does not take bookings for it)
notes: The single seasonal tasting menu, with Bresse poultry and Jura cheeses (Friday dinner to Saturday dinner only)
verdict: The third star on the Jura list and the only one where the gastronomic menu runs on two days a week, so plan the grand night for Friday or Saturday. Gault&Millau 2026 gives 13.5/20 and says Barberot is changing the house gradually. The weekday bistrot is the easier, cheaper way in. It is a long drive from Lons for dinner: pair it with Pasteur's Dole by day.
caveat: About 50 km north of Lons (A39); the starred menu only Friday evening to Saturday evening, bistrot the rest of the week; phone not verified

name: Ô Tablier
tier: THE BERTHS · LONS AT TABLE — THE TOWN'S OWN KITCHENS
recognition: Gault&Millau 2026: selected (no score), one of five Lons restaurants in the guide
what_to_order: Croûte aux morilles au Vin Jaune|Fondue|Roast duck fillet with Macvin|Apple brick with smoked raclette|Goat's cheese and chocolate dessert|Comté and Macvin ice cream
price_range: About 36-42 euros a head without drinks (seen Oct 2026, Gault&Millau)
notes: Croûte aux morilles au Vin Jaune
verdict: The most local cooking inside Lons, at prices that suit a crew lunch, but it is a modest bistro, not a destination: Gault&Millau selects it without a score. The room is tiny and the opening hours are irregular and disputed, so phone the same morning. Order the morel crust and whatever Jura white the cellar suggests.
caveat: Tiny room; closed Wednesday and Sunday, dinner only some days; hours differ between listings, call first

name: La Petite Auberge
tier: LONS AT TABLE — THE TOWN'S OWN KITCHENS
recognition: Gault&Millau: 11/20 (2025 review), still in the guide's Lons selection
what_to_order: Croûte aux morilles et Vin Jaune|Jura trout with roasted bacon|Menu des Gourmets|Soufflé glacé au Macvin|Griottines de Fougerolles
price_range: About 22-47 euros a head without drinks; Menu des Gourmets 47 euros (seen Oct 2026, Gault&Millau; the English page shows 32-45)
reservation: Phone to book and confirm the day
verdict: A safe traditional dinner close to town, rated 11/20 by Gault&Millau, with the 47 euro Menu des Gourmets as the full tour. Diner reviews are mixed: an August 2026 TripAdvisor review complained of a cool welcome and prices, while others praise the cooking. Go for the classics and the soufflé, not for a polished service.
caveat: Hours disputed between listings (Saturday especially); a car or taxi from the centre; reviews mention cool service

name: Le Bistrot des Marronniers
tier: LONS AT TABLE — THE TOWN'S OWN KITCHENS
recognition: Gault&Millau 2026: in the guide as a traditional regional brasserie, market menu 37.95 euros
what_to_order: Tablier de sapeur|Oeuf cocotte, Comté and Macvin sauce|Croûte aux champignons|Quenelle de brochet|Grilled meat from the wood stove|Market menu
reservation: Phone; walk-in possible outside business-lunch hours
notes: Meat from the wood-fired grill, or the pike quenelle
verdict: A reliable, generous table rather than a fine one: Gault&Millau's 2026 entry keeps it in the guide with a market menu at 37.95 euros, and recent reviews praise the welcome. Order from the fire or the pike quenelle. Hours vary between listings, but it serves both lunch and dinner on most weekdays, which makes it the easiest booking in town.
caveat: Closed Sunday; Monday and Saturday hours disputed between listings; busy with business lunches

name: La Finette, Taverne d'Arbois
tier: ARBOIS AT TABLE — THE TAVERN AND THE CAVE À MANGER
recognition: Gault&Millau 2026: 11/20, 'Table Gourmande'; in the Jura tavern trade since 1961
what_to_order: Fondue au Comté|Volaille au Vin Jaune et morilles|Saucisse de Morteau|Jura trout|Franche-Comté ice cream with Fougerolles cherries|A bottle from the all-Jura list
price_range: About 30-57 € a head without drinks (Gault&Millau 2026, seen Oct 2026)
notes: Poulet (volaille) au Vin Jaune et morilles
verdict: Go for the room and the classics, not for finesse. Gault&Millau 2026 gives it 11/20 and says the technique does not always convince, probably because of the crowds, while praising the terrace, the mood and generous plates. Diners rate it highly on Google (4.6 from about 2,700 reviews). Order the fondue or the Vin Jaune chicken and drink a local bottle.
caveat: In Arbois, about 40 km north of Lons by road; busy at weekends and in season, so book; hours vary by source, call ahead
hot_this_month: Open every day by its record: fondue de Comté and poulet au Vin Jaune et morilles for a cold November evening.

name: Le Bistrot des Claquets
tier: ARBOIS AT TABLE — THE TAVERN AND THE CAVE À MANGER
recognition: Listed by Le Fooding as Arbois's natural-wine cave à manger; June 2026 reviews on Raisin
what_to_order: Plat du jour|Cold-starter buffet|Entrée-plat-dessert formula|Aperitif board of regional charcuterie and cheese|Jura natural wine by the glass or bottle
price_range: Plates about 12 €, formulas 16-19.50 € (Le Fooding, undated; seen Oct 2026)
reservation: Lunch by phone only; walk-ins possible if there is room
notes: The plat du jour with the cold-starter buffet, and a glass from the shelf
verdict: The cheapest serious lunch on the Arbois side and the easiest place to drink Arbois natural wine without an appointment. There is no choice at lunch, which is the point. June 2026 visitors on Raisin praise the room and the value. Book by phone for lunch; the tables go fast.
caveat: Lunch booking by phone only; closed Sunday and Monday; posted autumn break 23 Oct-1 Nov (year not stated); about 40 km from Lons

name: Marché de Lons-le-Saunier
address: Place de Verdun and Place du 11 Novembre (Thursday); Cours Sully (Saturday), 39000 Lons-le-Saunier
tier: THE BERTHS · LA RUE — THE MARKET, THE FROMAGER AND THE CHOCOLATIER
recognition: Thursday is the largest market in the Jura department; Saturday morning organic food market
what_to_order: Comté at several ages|Mont d'Or AOP|Saucisse de Morteau IGP|Cancoillotte|Bleu de Gex|Miel de sapin
notes: Comté at two or three ages from one stall, and a Mont d'Or for the boat oven
verdict: Thursday morning is the one to plan around: the food stalls are on Place de Verdun and thin out by midday. Saturday is the quieter, greener version. The new mayor, elected in March 2026, has tested moving the Thursday market to Place de la Liberté and rue du Commerce, so check the squares before you go.
caveat: Thursday food is mornings only; a permanent move to Place de la Liberté is under study, check the location
hot_this_month: Mont d'Or back on the cheese stalls, on sale since 10 September; four Thursday markets in November, 5 to 26.

name: Chez l'Artisan Fromager
tier: LA RUE — THE MARKET, THE FROMAGER AND THE CHOCOLATIER
recognition: The Poulet family, cheesemakers for four generations, selling their own Morbier, raclette and tomme du Jura
reservation: Walk-in; ask a day ahead for a large order
verdict: The best-evidenced cheese counter in central Lons and the right replacement for a Comté affineur the old guide placed here by mistake. Come for the Morbier, which is the family's own; for a run of Comté ages, the Thursday market stalls may serve you better. Hours conflict and nothing dated 2026 turned up, so check before carrying a cool bag across town.
caveat: Hours conflict between directories and no 2026-dated evidence was found: call or pass by first

name: Chocolaterie Pelen
tier: LA RUE — THE MARKET, THE FROMAGER AND THE CHOCOLATIER
recognition: Family chocolatier since 1899, roasts its own beans; listed by Gault&Millau as an artisan
what_to_order: Écureuil|Galet de Chalain|Chocolate from house-roasted beans|Praliné bonbons|Ice cream
price_range: Pastries and chocolates, about 3-8 € a piece in May 2026 (not re-checked)
notes: The écureuil, and the Galet de Chalain praliné-nougatine
verdict: The chocolate shop Lons is known for, and the place for an edible gift to carry back aboard. Gault&Millau lists it as an artisan. Recent reviews are mixed: praise for the pastries and the écureuil, complaints about prices, early closing and a cool welcome, with a newer note that the tea room has improved. Buy the chocolate; do not count on a late coffee.
caveat: The shop is 1 rue Saint-Désiré in the centre; rue Blaise Pascal is the industrial-zone site. Tea room closes early
